paragraphs: Here's what I love, friend. Before the LORD acts, He lets Abraham in on it. He says He has chosen Abraham so that he will command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD "by doing what is right and just" (Genesis 18:19). So when Abraham stays standing before the LORD, he's doing just what he was chosen for, and I think that's why he cares so much about what is right.

Now look at what Abraham asks. "Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?" (Genesis 18:25). He doesn't ask it like a man picking a fight. He asks it like someone who knows the LORD, and he keeps going from fifty down to ten, with a humble "I am but dust and ashes" (Genesis 18:27) and a "May the Lord not be angry" (Genesis 18:30) along the way. And every time, the LORD answers him. The LORD hears a humble man who cares about other people, and He doesn't brush him off.

So here's your takeaway, baker. You can bring the LORD your biggest concerns for other people, and you can do it humbly and honestly, again and again. Abraham asks six times, and the door never closes on him. I'd say that's an invitation to pray for the people around you. And keep that apron on, friend, because this story is NOT done.
